I have more work incoming, but I can't yet say when I'll be upstreaming it, it's for a device we have in development.

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7467

Well, the attribute is there for a reason obviously, the struct really needs to be packed.
How do I fix that for Windows? (I'm a Linux guy)

Is this the way to do it?
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1537964/visual-c-equivalent-of-gccs-attribute-packed

The problem is not the only change for windows. That is a solution I found as well, but the issue is a little bit bigger.

You have to ensure that it works on gcc, clang, msvc as well as Apple, macOS and Windows. I currently cannot verify that the  above mentioned solution may work on clang-llvm  (@guyharris could you way in here? You have more knowledge about that stuff). The solution from stackoverflow seems to me "a little bit" too easy.
I'll try it tonight on macos, and if that works i'll submit it as a solution (already verified it would work on Windows and Linux).
AFAIK clang supports this attribute

From just reading the documentation, I would second that. Just no way to verify atm. 

Btw, this is not your fault. Our buildsystem should have caught it. That is another issue, and one that actually scares me a bit more. It exists for a reason and not having it perform such an essential check is a little bit worrisome.

No worries, we get the dissector fixed in no time, but the windows builds must work

I can submit a PR fixing it as well.
I'll (now) verify that it works on a clang build (on Linux).

Even better, that would work and we just check macos and Solaris after the fact. If clang is ok with it, generally speaking, macos should be as well. The arm version might complain, but that I can check tonight

Works on my gcc 12 and clang 14 Linux builds.

See https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7470
I'm sorry about the breakage. I did see it but assumed it was not my code because all the CI builds were ok.
Hey, thats ok. To create stuff, sometimes you have to break stuff. I am just annoyed that the CI builds did not catch it. They should have.
I don't understand why the packed struct is necessary. Is this not the same as `#define SAMPLE_SET_SIZE 34`?

My guess is (and having seen the same thing in automation), the data has the first entry as 2 byte, the rest as 4-byte. Usually what happens is, that compilers are optimizing to align for 4 byte addresses, and in this case the data is transmitted as displayed in the packed struct. So therefore the alignment is off after the first uin16_t.

What you usually do though is pack the struct to apply by stacking up the entries manually. Only if you create a new protocol though is this a possibility.

Yes I could do that too.
Is it ok to do that as a follow-up?

Obviously, we used some internal code snippets to build the dissector, this is one of them.
I would be fine by that, @jvalverde you agree?

Yes, I agree.

I assume the struct was used as documentation but as a matter of policy we don't require any particular compiler or compiler extension to build Wireshark so the use of the attribute should be removed.

Yeah, we are currently investigating the issue. In any case, it is not caused by the integration of your dissector code.
